args.title: Prove time is right: the clock scan and the month-end, year-end, restore and two-world tests
args.why: Aaron settled devnet.site-follows-world for option A on 10 November 2026 and said the time has to be right. A mistake shows up as a document dated by the machine, often unnoticed until a month end, so each proof is a run. Only two of six tests exist in the spike.
args.what: Build the six tests of decision devnet.time-is-right: (1) the scan that fails the build when a pinned app adds an unlabelled direct read of the machine's clock, with the committed list of the direct reads; (2) a month end where every ledger date equals the world's date; (3) a jump across a fiscal year with the next year created first; (4) a restore to an earlier snapshot with job counts; (5) two worlds at different times on one bench, also under load from one worker; (6) a person's session across an advance. Add the gaps beside them: past-world log retention, every scheduled job once per period across a 60-day jump, an upgrade rehearsal. Make the direct reads that decide something point at the world's clock, switch log clean-up off in worlds, and propose the seam to Frappe upstream.
doneWhen: The scan exists, is in the checks and fails on an unlabelled direct read; the committed list labels every direct read.
The month-end, fiscal-year, restore and two-world tests run and pass, each as an eval of the book, on a bench with the clock seam; the restore test counts jobs.
The session rule (a one-day step keeps a signed-in session, a step past its lifetime ends it with a message) is a passing test.
The coordinator's re-run of the clock checks has passed.

args.why: Time comes first: Aaron said it has to be right, and he settled the approach for option A, so the proof of it is the first thing built on it. The spikes' evidence is in the book, so the contract reconciliation follows; the machine is the one step only Aaron can unblock, so it is asked for early.
